text: Iran widens Gulf attacks by targeting a US air base in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain. CAIRO (AP) — Iran widened its attacks on its Gulf neighbors on Wednesday, targeting a US air base in Kuwait and launching several attacks on Bahrain in what appeared to be retaliation for American strikes the day before. After about two months without such attacks, Iran has repeatedly targeted US facilities in Bahrain in recent days. The small Persian Gulf island kingdom hosts the US Navy’s 5th Fleet. The early morning attacks came after a US fighter jet struck a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site Tuesday on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The US strike was in retaliation for an Iranian attack on an American radar installation in Bahrain earlier Tuesday. Iran said that its recent attacks — including those on other US facilities in Bahrain on Sunday and Friday — were in response to US drone surveillance operations and an attack on Iranian communications towers. The uptick in fighting with the tit-for-tat attacks raises the risk of further escalation toward the resumption of all-out conflict nearly nine months into the war, and complicates negotiations for a diplomatic solution, which have stagnated despite intensified mediation efforts from Qatar. The US military didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment on the latest attacks. ## Blockade puts pressure on Tehran With its economy suffering under a US naval blockade and American military escorts helping restore the passage of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, experts say that the recent attacks suggest Tehran may be growing weary of the status quo. “Even if neither side intends to enter a broader confrontation, the accumulation of military incidents across multiple fronts increases the risk of miscalculation and escalation beyond what either side originally intended,” Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group think tank, wrote in an analysis posted to X following the initial reports of the attack on Kuwait. US President Donald Trump has sent mixed messages on his next steps, saying new strikes are highly unlikely, but also sending a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the Middle East. Though US military protection has helped restore oil shipments from the Gulf, Iran has continued to attack tankers as they attempt to transit the Strait of Hormuz. United Arab Emirates state-owned oil company ADNOC said Wednesday that one of its tanker crew members was missing after an attack in the strait on Tuesday, while 11 others were injured and were receiving medical care. Danny Citrinowicz, a researcher at Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies and a former Iran specialist in Israel’s military and intelligence services, described an “increasingly clear” pattern of attacks by Iran on shipping and US facilities in the Gulf region. “Iran appears to be pursuing a strategy of deliberate, calibrated escalation,” he wrote in an analysis on X. “The objective is not necessarily to trigger an all-out war, but to steadily increase the military, economic, and political costs of maintaining the blockade.” He said that Washington is faced with the dilemma that a limited response may encourage Iran to push further, while a stronger response risks accelerating the escalation that the US is trying to avoid. “As long as the US naval blockade remains in place and no agreement is reached, further escalation will become increasingly difficult to avoid,” he said. “There are two clear paths to de-escalation: a negotiated agreement or a US decision to lift the blockade.” ## Iran renews attacks on American bases After Israel and the US attacked Iran on Feb. 28 to launch the war, Iran regularly fired on American facilities and interests in neighboring Gulf countries, as well as energy infrastructure and other targets. In the attack early Wednesday on the Ali Al Salem air base in Kuwait, the Iranian military fired at air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms, according to a report on Iran’s state broadcaster. Kuwait’s military said that its air defenses had intercepted drone attacks and didn’t immediately report any damage. The Kuwaiti Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated Iranian attacks as “criminal,” saying that they threatened the country’s security and stability. During the war, Ali Al Salem Air Base has been struck at least 30 times by Iran, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, numerous warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area, according to an analysis by The Associated Press. The AP’s analysis used satellite imagery from multiple providers to help determine that Iran’s strikes on more than two dozen US bases in the Middle East focused on early-warning systems before hitting aircraft and buildings, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage. AP also spoke to four regional officials who were briefed or had firsthand knowledge of what was hit. The AP found that, through August, more than 115 drone or missile strikes claimed by Iran or Iranian-backed militias damaged or destroyed structures on 26 military bases and other sites with US equipment. Under questioning before a US Senate committee Tuesday about damage to the Navy’s regional headquarters in Bahrain, Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said he couldn’t offer a full damage assessment in Bahrain because “it’s a nonpermissive area for us to go.” He told a reporter months ago that Iran “blew the hell out of Bahrain.” Meanwhile, Bahrain’s Interior Ministry issued two alerts early Wednesday urging people to take shelter, followed by the “all clear” a short time later. The country’s military later said that it had intercepted a number of attacks from Iran, but gave no information on any damage or casualties. ## Houthis target Riyadh after deadly coalition strikes Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles fired toward the capital, Riyadh, by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, according to Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis. Alerts also sounded in three other Saudi cities. Civil defense authorities later said that the danger had passed, but provided no further details. The previous day, coalition forces launched a major air attack across rebel-held areas of Yemen that the Houthis said killed at least 17 people. Al-Malki said that Tuesday’s strikes destroyed “60 legitimate military targets” and aimed to weaken the Houthis’ missile and drone capabilities. The strikes followed the withdrawal of Saudi-backed forces from areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a setback for the anti-Houthi camp. The withdrawal consolidated the Houthis’ grip on the strategic waterway, which is crucial to international trade and global oil shipments. *Rising reported from Bangkok.*
